newsitem.title: USA: New England utilities warn of possible shortages.
newsitem.headline: New England utilities warn of possible shortages.

text.p: New England power companies warned Wednesday that electric power shortages of around 2,000 megawatts may occur in the region this summer in the event of an extended heatwave.
The expected outage of four major generating stations, continued economic growth and hot weather may cause power shortages, the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL) said Wednesday.
Regional peak demand is forecast to reach 21,400 MW during hot weather this summer, above the peak demand forecast last year of 21,000 MW and the all-time peak of 20,519 MW in the summer of 1994.

The net generating capacity of the power companies this summer, including power purchases, is 26,800 MW. But taking into consideration already known generator outages, totalling 3,430 MW, and an allowance of 2,400 MW for unplanned outages, there is the potential for power shortages of around 2,000 MW, the companies said.
The companies have proposed adding 450 MW of additional generating capacity by reactivating mothballed generators and increasing output at some generators.
The utilities will also be working with large customers to obtain "interruptable load contracts" for periods when electrical demand is especially high, the companies said.
The utilities will also work closely with neighboring power systems in New York, Quebec and New Brunswick to improve the ability to purchase additional power.
If conditions seriously deteriorate, the utilities can also disconnect customers for a short period of time on a rotating basis, the companies said.
